title: Illustrations
summary: --Illustrations is a free-floating subdivision ($v for collections, $x for discussions) used only under types of published materials, literatures and literary forms, names of individual persons (for illustrations of their written works), individual works (author-title or uniform title), and sacred works and their parts. Under other headings use --Pictorial works, not --Illustrations. Technique of illustration takes phrase headings (Illustration of books, Medical illustration, etc.). LC now uses only the topical $x form, with LCGFT Illustrated works for collections.
validation_rules: `--Illustrations` is coded $v for collections of illustrations and $x for discussions of illustrations. (H 1659 sec. A)
`--Illustrations` is free-floating under types of published materials, e.g. `Newspapers--Illustrations` ($x), `Paperbacks--Illustrations` ($v). (H 1659 sec. D)

`--Illustrations` is free-floating under literatures and literary forms, e.g. `English literature--Illustrations`, `Nursery rhymes, English--Illustrations`, `Adventure stories--Illustrations`. (H 1659 sec. E, J)

`--Illustrations` is free-floating under names of individual persons for pictorial representations of the person's written works, e.g. `Shakespeare, William, 1564-1616--Illustrations`, `Josephus, Flavius--Illustrations`. (H 1659 sec. F)

`--Illustrations` is free-floating under individual works (author-title or uniform title entries), e.g. `Beowulf--Illustrations`, `Milton, John, 1608-1674. Paradise lost--Illustrations`. (H 1659 sec. G.1)

`--Illustrations` is free-floating under uniform titles for sacred works and their individual parts, e.g. `Bible. Revelation--Illustrations`, `Qur'an--Illustrations`; used for illustrated editions, collections without text, and discussions. (H 1659 sec. G.2)
Do not use `--Illustrations` under other types of headings (e.g. ordinary topics, places); use `--Pictorial works` instead (H 1935). (H 1659 sec. H)
Works on the technique of making illustrations take phrase headings, e.g. `Caricature`, `Illustration of books`, `Medical illustration`, `Scientific illustration`. (H 1659 sec. I)

A work on illustrations of a medieval romance about a person may combine `--Romances--Illustrations` under the personal name, e.g. `Alexander, the Great, 356 B.C.-323 B.C.--Romances--Illustrations`. (H 1659 sec. J)

[LC practice] LC uses only the topical `$x Illustrations` for discussions; for collections LC assigns the heading without the subdivision plus LCGFT `Illustrated works`. The $v form remains valid LCSH. (H 1659 sec. A, D-G)

sections.heading: A. Background
sections.text:
The subdivision *--Illustrations* is used as a form or topical subdivision under types of published materials, literatures, literary forms, names of individual persons, individual works, and sacred works for collections or discussions of pictorial representations found in these works or depicting these subjects. This instruction sheet provides guidelines for using this subdivision. The subdivision is coded as a $v subfield for collections of illustrations or as an $x subfield for discussions of illustrations.

LC practice: As stated in H 1075, LC catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT), e.g. *Illustrated works*.

For guidelines on place as a theme in art, see H 910. For guidelines on art and fine art, see H 1250. For guidelines on artistic photography, see H 1255. For guidelines on pictorial works, see H 1935. For guidelines on exhibitions, see H 1593.

sections.heading: B. Recent revisions
sections.text: 2026-04: Updated template. Added instructions related to LCGFT implementation.

sections.heading: C. Definition
sections.text: Illustrations: Pictorial representations in published materials.

sections.heading: D. Types of published materials
sections.text:
Use the free-floating subdivision *--Illustrations* under types of published materials for collections or discussions of illustrations used in these publications.

LC practice: Use the free-floating topical subdivision *--Illustrations* under types of published materials for discussions of illustrations used in these publications. For collections of illustrations in these publications, assign a subject heading for the type of published materials and the topic, if applicable. Assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand.

Examples:

```
650 #0 $a Newspapers $x Illustrations.
650 #0 $a Paperbacks $v Illustrations.
LC practice for collections of illustrations:
650 #0 $a Paperbacks.
655 #7 $a Illustrated works. $2 lcgft
```

sections.heading: E. Literature
sections.text:
Use the free-floating form subdivision *--Illustrations* under literatures and literary forms for collections of pictorial representations of literary subjects. For discussion of these topics, use the free-floating topical subdivision.

LC practice: Use the free-floating topical subdivision *--Illustrations* under literatures and literary forms for discussions of pictorial representations of these literary subjects. For collections of illustrations, assign a subject heading for the type of literature and the topic, if applicable. Assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand.

Examples:

```
650 #0 $a English literature $x Illustrations.
650 #0 $a Nursery rhymes, English $x Illustrations.
LC practice for collections of illustrations:
650 #0 $a English literature.
650 #0 $a Nursery rhymes, English.
655 #7 $a Illustrated works. $2 lcgft
```

sections.heading: F. Individual persons
sections.text:
Use the free-floating form subdivision *--Illustrations* under names of individual persons for collections of pictorial representations of the person's written works. For discussion of these topics, use the free-floating topical subdivision.

LC practice: Use the free-floating topical subdivision *--Illustrations* under names of individual persons for discussions of pictorial representations of the person's written works. For collections of illustrations, assign a subject heading for the individual persons and the topic, if applicable. Assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand.

Examples:

```
600 10 $a Shakespeare, William $d 1564-1616 $v Illustrations.
600 10 $a Josephus, Flavius $x Illustrations.
LC practice for collections of illustrations:
600 10 $a Shakespeare, William $d 1564-1616.
655 #7 $a Illustrated works. $2 lcgft
```

sections.heading: G.1. General
sections.text:
Use the free-floating form subdivision *--Illustrations* under individual works (author-title or uniform title entries) for collections of pictorial representations of these works without text. For discussion of these topics, use the free-floating topical subdivision.

LC practice: Use the free-floating topical subdivision *--Illustrations* under individual works (author-title or uniform title entries) for discussions of these illustrations. For collections of pictorial representations of these works, assign a subject heading for the individual works and the topic, if applicable. Assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand.

Examples:

```
630 00 $a Beowulf $x Illustrations.
600 10 $a Milton, John, $d 1608-1674. $t Paradise lost $v Illustrations.
LC practice for collections of illustrations:
600 10 $a Milton, John, $d 1608-1674. $t Paradise lost.
655 #7 $a Illustrated works. $2 lcgft
```

sections.heading: G.2. Sacred works
sections.text:
Use the free-floating form subdivision *--Illustrations* under uniform titles for sacred works and their individual parts for collections of pictorial representations of these works. For discussion of these topics, use the free-floating topical subdivision.

Assign a heading of this type to illustrated editions of sacred works, to collections of such illustrations without text, and to discussions of these illustrations.

LC practice: Use the free-floating topical subdivision *--Illustrations* under uniform titles for sacred works and their individual parts for discussions of pictorial representations of these works. This includes illustrated editions of sacred works, collections of such illustrations without text, and to discussions of these illustrations. For collections of pictorial representations of these works, assign a subject heading for the individual works and the topic, if applicable. Assign LCGFT appropriate to the form and/or genre of the resource in hand.

Example:

```
630 00 $a Bible. $p Revelation $v Illustrations.
630 00 $a Qur'an $x Illustrations.
LC practice for collections of illustrations:
630 00 $a Bible. $p Revelation.
655 #7 $a Illustrated works. $2 lcgft
```

sections.heading: H. Other
sections.text:
In accordance with H 1935, use the subdivision *--Pictorial works* under other types of headings for collections of pictorial representations of these subjects. Do not use the subdivision *--Illustrations* under these topics.

LC practice: For guidelines on pictorial works, see H 1935.

sections.heading: I. Technique
sections.text:
To works discussing the technique of making illustrations, assign the appropriate phrase heading, if one exists or can be established.

Example:

```
650 #0 $a Caricature.
650 #0 $a Illustration of books.
650 #0 $a Medical illustration.
650 #0 $a Scientific illustration.
```
